title: Normalized scalar and Frobenius counit conclusion data
statement: Fix the normalized scalar realization family of [def-sf-adic-realization-isomorphism-data], the separated finite-type models and chosen geometric compactification of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], and the actual ordinary categories and canonical mate predicates of [def-sf-native-weil-scalar-counit-categories]. Use the coefficient construction [def-sf-constructible-exceptional-coefficient-construction-data], the common-field functors and normalized adjunction [lem-sf-exceptional-field-descent], and actual native section operations [lem-sf-locally-finite-adic-compact-support-realization]. Define conclusion data, not an existence assertion: two equivalences whose forward functors equal the recorded realization; a natural scalar compact-support comparison; its constructible preservation and left-adjoint identification normalized by that comparison and equivalence counit; preservation under both Frobenius pullbacks and their inverses; forward and inverse exchange isomorphisms satisfying the canonical cancellation square; invertibility of their actual right mate, its explicit counit equation and the invariant equation for every native derived Weil object. Define its Frobenius normalization by equality with the recorded common-stage geometric comparison and the typed realization and restriction squares. Define its scalar normalization by the actual integral proper/open mate normalization, specified source and target scalar maps, a bridge from the fixed common compact-support functor to its coefficient-construction stage action whose components are the inverses of the recorded rationalLeft comparisons at every finite coefficient stage, the canonical section transport equality composed through that bridge, and shift compatibility. The coefficient changes and separately derived proper/open image are those of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. All these fields are data/properties to be supplied as conclusions; none asserts an unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoint.
